evidence: src/domain/order-state.ts: ORDER_STATES, nextState and canCancelFrom are the only place the transition rules are written down.
src/domain/order.ts: advance() and moveTo() both use nextState(this.currentState), and cancel() uses canCancelFrom. Neither repeats the state ordering.
src/domain/order-line.ts: the OrderLine constructor holds the one positive-integer quantity check.
src/domain/product.ts: canReserve(quantity) holds the availability check, and reserve() and release() keep the available/reserved counts in step.
src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts: reserve() calls product.canReserve and product.reserve through the ProductRepository port. It does not change stock fields directly.
src/domain/domain-errors.ts: NotFoundError, InvalidRequestError, InsufficientStockError and InvalidTransitionError all extend DomainError, and every other file uses them.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit covers one concern: orders and product stock in an order-fulfillment domain. It has the entities Order, OrderLine and Product. The state sequence and transition functions live in order-state.ts. It has repository ports (OrderRepository, ProductRepository), an IdGenerator port, one shared error hierarchy and one domain service (StockReservationService). Each rule lives in one place. The state order and transition rules are only in order-state.ts (nextState, canCancelFrom). Order.advance and Order.moveTo both call nextState and do not re-encode the order. The positive-quantity rule is only in the OrderLine constructor. The stock-availability check is only in Product.canReserve. StockReservationService calls product.canReserve in its pre-check pass and then product.reserve, so it works through Product rather than changing stock fields directly. It loads products through the ProductRepository port. Every error extends DomainError in domain-errors.ts. One minor point: Order.advance and Order.moveTo repeat the same cancelled-flag guard inside one class. That is a small amount of repeated code, not a rule split across files. Nothing splits into unrelated concerns or works around the module's own types and functions.
